summary: Third consecutive fully silent week — zero messages from either side, again. The chat's last message of any kind is Stephski's 8/4 nudge, so this thread has now been dead for 24 straight days, and Hannah (Bella) herself has been silent for 53 days since she announced her exit on 7/6. Every action item flagged last week was ignored: the 7/1-7/7 final invoice is still unissued (now 44 days past ALTR's own 7/15 cadence date), the exit balance she volunteered to pay is still uncollected, and nobody has yet opened the 7/6 screenshot (message id 316, captioned "This is total left") that is the only record anywhere of what she owes. A separate and uglier fact surfaced on a full re-read of the history: her churn message was never answered by anyone. Not once. The next two messages in the chat after she quit were Mica's routine reel inspo and Michelle's weekly leak-removal report on 7/10 — business as usual, four days after the client said she was leaving. ALTR is carrying an unquantified receivable against an ex-client on a dead channel, with no owner, and has now spent three weeks doing nothing about it.

health.rationale: Drops from 5 to 3 on a third straight zero-message week. The 2-point fall is small only because there is almost nothing left to lose: the client churned 53 days ago and the score now measures collectability, not relationship health. What moved it down is that every specific recommendation from the 8/21 file was ignored — the invoice was not issued (44 days past cadence), no off-Telegram escalation was attempted, and the one cheap action available (read the 7/6 screenshot and write the number down) still has not been done. Three weeks of documented ALTR-side inaction on a live receivable is a deterioration, not a plateau. The recommended write-off date of 2026-09-04 is now 7 days out and will arrive with the account in exactly the same state it was in on 8/14.

payments.note: No movement, no contact, no invoice — third week running. Two items are outstanding and NEITHER has a number attached anywhere in the written record: (1) the final 7/1-7/7 commission invoice, never issued, 44 days past its 7/15 cadence date; (2) the exit balance she volunteered on 7/6, whose only record is an untranscribed screenshot (message id 316). The last stated dollar figures in the chat are historical payments already collected — $931.81 on 6/23 covering 5/29-6/14, and $981 on 7/6 covering 6/15-6/30, both after she deducted her self-run live earnings. Extrapolating from the 6/15-6/30 invoice ($981 at ALTR's 35% rate implies roughly $2,800 net over 16 days), a 7-day final period puts the unissued invoice in the rough range of $400-500. That is an ALTR-side estimate only and is NOT stated anywhere in the chat. Her payment behaviour was consistently good: she paid every invoice she was actually sent, within days, and she raised the exit balance herself unprompted. The blocker has never been her willingness to pay.

suggestions: This is the third week this file has asked for a decision and the third week nothing happened. Put a single name against this account today. Option A (recommended): read the 7/6 screenshot, issue the 7/1-7/7 invoice from ALTR's own OF records (est. $400-500 plus whatever the screenshot shows), send it once off Telegram with a 14-day pay-by date. Option B: write it off on 2026-09-04 as previously recommended — that date is 7 days away — and close the account. Doing neither, which is what has happened for 21 straight days, is the only genuinely bad outcome.

Read message id 316 from 2026-07-06 ("This is total left" + photo). This was the number-one recommendation in the 8/21 file and it is still outstanding. It costs about thirty seconds. You cannot make a write-off decision on a figure nobody has looked at, and right now the size of this receivable is unknown to the business.

Stop using Telegram for this. The chat has produced zero client replies in 53 days and its last message of any kind is 24 days old. She gave a phone number in-chat on 6/4 (407-587-9986) and her OF account email on 5/29 ([REDACTED-RECOVERY-EMAIL]). She was also referred by Vale, who is an active ALTR client — a warm ask through the referrer is the highest-probability channel left, and it is the only one that has not been tried.

Fix the process failure that this chat exposes, independent of the money: a client announced she was leaving on 7/6 and not one of the seven ALTR people in that group replied. Mica sent reel inspo and Michelle sent a leak report four days later as if the account were live. There is no churn-notification trigger and no owner for exiting clients. That is a systems gap that will repeat on the next churn, and it is worth more than the $400-500 sitting in this thread.

Log the churn root causes into the retention playbook and remove this account from the weekly client rotation: weak week-1 subscriber numbers (Fred, 5/30: 'we're on 4 subs today so far... yesterday and days before there's been an average of 60-70 subscribers a day'), a billing dispute over commission on her self-run lives, three bank/payment-rail changes in five weeks (Zelle → Mercury → Chase → Bank of America), and leaks she kept reporting as still live. A churned client with an unowned receivable belongs on a collections list, not in a client-care report.
